ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-08-15
Provider: Dr. Lisa Thompson, MD
Department: Allergy & Immunology
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Frequent bacterial pneumonia and otitis media recurring shortly after antibiotic courses completed.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient returns for ongoing management of his complex history including severe combined immunodeficiency, cystic fibrosis, and recently evaluated severe aplastic anemia and vascular ring. Since he was around 6 months old, he has had multiple episodes of otitis media and bacterial pneumonia requiring antibiotics. His parents report that he recovers with treatment but often gets sick again within a few weeks. He is up to date on routine pediatric visits but has not received live vaccines.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Severe combined immunodeficiency (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Cystic fibrosis (diagnosed 2020-03-15)
- Severe aplastic anemia (diagnosed 2020-05-15)
- Vascular ring (diagnosed 2020-07-15)
- Severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID)
- X-linked agammaglobulinemia (Bruton disease)
- Transient hypogammaglobulinemia of infancy
- Glycogen storage disease type V (McArdle disease)
- Congenital vascular ring
- Cleft palate
- Failure to thrive
- Recurrent respiratory infections

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Cleft palate repair (scheduled)
- Vascular ring ligation and division (pending cardiothoracic evaluation)

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Immune globulin (IVIG) 400 mg/kg IV infusion monthly
- Pancrelipase (Creon) 3000 units lipase per 120 mL of formula or breast milk
- Uncooked cornstarch 1.6 g/kg orally every 4 hours while awake
- Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 5 mg/kg TMP component orally once daily (prophylaxis)
- Cyclosporine 10 mg/kg/day orally divided BID (for bone marrow suppression)

ALLERGIES:
No known drug allergies

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Maternal uncle: deceased at age 2 from severe infections (suspected X-linked immunodeficiency)
- First cousin (maternal): cystic fibrosis
- Parents: distant consanguinity (third cousins)
- Older sibling: healthy, no chronic medical conditions

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: None (infant).

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On physical examination, he appears well-nourished and interactive. No tonsillar tissue is visualized, and cervical lymph nodes are not palpable.

LABORATORY DATA:
Laboratory results reveal markedly reduced levels of all major immunoglobulin classes. T cell counts are within normal limits.

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2021-07-15
Provider: Dr. Robert Kim, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Acute episode of shakiness, sweating, and irritability upon awakening with progressive abdominal distension.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
This 1-year-old male with severe combined immunodeficiency, cystic fibrosis, severe aplastic anemia, and congenital vascular ring followed in multiple subspecialty clinics presents to the emergency department. The parents report that the baby tires easily during feeding, becomes irritable when meals are delayed, and occasionally appears shaky or sweaty in the early morning. Over the past two months, the infant has failed to gain weight adequately, and his abdomen has become visibly enlarged. There is no vomiting or diarrhea.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Severe combined immunodeficiency (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Cystic fibrosis (diagnosed 2020-03-15)
- Severe aplastic anemia (diagnosed 2020-05-15)
- Vascular ring (diagnosed 2020-07-15)
- X-linked (Bruton) agammaglobulinemia (diagnosed 2020-08-15)
- Transient hypogammaglobulinemia of infancy (diagnosed 2021-01-15)
- Severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID)
- X-linked agammaglobulinemia (Bruton disease)
- Glycogen storage disease type V (McArdle disease)
- Congenital vascular ring
- Cleft palate
- Failure to thrive
- Recurrent respiratory infections

His vaccinations are up to date,.

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Cleft palate repair (scheduled)
- Vascular ring ligation and division (pending cardiothoracic evaluation)

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Immune globulin (IVIG) 400 mg/kg IV infusion monthly
- Pancrelipase (Creon) 3000 units lipase per 120 mL of formula or breast milk
- Uncooked cornstarch 1.6 g/kg orally every 4 hours while awake
- Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 5 mg/kg TMP component orally once daily (prophylaxis)
- Cyclosporine 10 mg/kg/day orally divided BID (for bone marrow suppression)

ALLERGIES:
No known drug allergies

FAMILY HISTORY:
There is no family history of metabolic disorders or early childhood deaths.

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: None (infant).

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On physical examination, the child appears alert but has a protuberant abdomen with hepatomegaly extending 4 cm below the right costal margin. Muscle tone is mildly decreased in the proximal limbs.

LABORATORY DATA:
Laboratory studies reveal mild hypoglycemia, elevated aspartate aminotransferase (AST), alanine aminotransferase (ALT), and a modest rise in creatine kinase. Lactic acid and uric acid levels are within normal limits.

PATHOLOGY:
A liver biopsy shows abnormal glycogen with short outer branches.
